2. Facts relevant for disposal of the appeal, in short, are that respondent Nos. 1 & 2. instituted Title Suit no.36 of 1991 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Kachua for declaration of title in 2.96 acres of land out of 4.44 acres appertaining to CS khatian No. 145, Mouza Badhai, PS Kachua, District-Bagerhat and also for a further declaration that the enlistment of the suit property as vested property to be illegal, void, ultra vires not binding upon the plaintiffs and also for a decree restraining the defendants permanently from dispossessing the plaintiffs from the suit property and also for a further relief for setting aside the exparte decree passed in Title Suit No 511 of 1983 of the First Munsifs Court. Bagerhat contending, inter alia, that the entire land of CS khatian No.145 measuring an area of 4.44 acres belonged to Darikanath and Rajkumar in equal shares. Darikanath died leaving behind only son named Krishnalal. Thereafter Rajkumar died leaving behind 2(two) sons named Mohendra and Dhirendra. It is the further case of the plaintiffs that 8(eight) annas share belonged to Mohendra and Dhirendra sold in auction in Money Execution Case No. 6 of 1950 and that auction was purchased by Krishnalal. This way Krishnalal became the owner and possessor in 16 annas share in the land of CS khatian No.145. Thereafter Krishnalal died leaving behind 3(three) sons, the plaintiff Nos. 1, 2 and the defendant No.9. The S.A. record was wrongly recorded in the name of Mohendra and Dhirendra. The plaintiffs came to know about the said fact when the defendant No. 1 disclosed about the same on 06.01.1990 and also about the exparte decree passed in Title Suit No. 511 of 1983. It is the further case of the plaintiffs that the defendant No.1 claimed that he got lease of eight annas share in the jote from the vested property authority vide lease case No.11(Ka)of 72-73 and as such the suit. 

 13. It is admitted that the total land measuring an area of 4.44 acres of khatian No. 145, mouja Badhal belonged to Darikanath and Rajkumar in equal shares. It is the plaintiffs' case that Rajkumar died leaving behind 2(two) sons named Mohendra and Dhirendra and their shares were sold in auction in money. Execution Case No. 6 of 1950. It is their further case that by that auction purchase, Krishnalal became the absolute owner and possessor in 4.44 acres and thereafter he died leaving behind the plaintiff Nos. 1 & 2 and the defendant No. 9 as his 3(three) sons. It is their case that amicably the plaintiffs have possession in 2.96 acres and the defendant No. 9 has possession in the rest 1.48 acres. Lastly their case is that the order treating of 2.22 acres as vested property is illegal in view of the fact that long before the promulgation of the law of Enemy Property, the shares of Mohendra & Darikanath were sold in auction.
